record.paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
record.original_question: For a one-dimensional Pisot inflation tiling with scaling factor λ, must the coincidence rank divide the algebraic norm of λ?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.2.3 (Coincidence Rank Conjecture) The coincidence rank of a one-dimensional Pisot inflation tiling must divide the algebraic norm of λ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let T be a one-dimensional primitive inflation tiling of the real line with inflation (scaling) factor λ, where λ is a Pisot number (a real algebraic integer greater than 1 all of whose Galois conjugates have modulus strictly less than 1). Let Ω be the associated tiling space (the orbit closure of T under translations) and let cr(Ω) denote the coincidence rank of the tiling, defined as the maximal cardinality of a collection of pairwise distinct tilings in Ω that share the same image under the maximal equicontinuous factor map (equivalently, the number of sheets of the canonical map from Ω to its maximal equicontinuous factor). Let N(λ) denote the absolute value of the algebraic norm of λ over ℚ, that is, the absolute value of the product of all Galois conjugates of λ.

Question: Must cr(Ω) divide N(λ)?
artifact.status_search_result: The Coincidence Rank Conjecture remains open in general. Partial results are known: Barge and collaborators have verified the conjecture when λ is a (rational) integer (degree one case) and for all Pisot λ when the coincidence rank equals 2. A weaker form—that the coincidence rank divides some power of the norm of λ—has also been studied via homological Pisot substitutions and the Exact Regularity Property. No proof of the full conjecture for general one-dimensional Pisot inflation tilings appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Factors of Pisot tiling spaces and the coincidence rank conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes partial results on the coincidence rank conjecture for Pisot inflation tilings.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is verified in special cases (e.g., coincidence rank 2, integer λ) but remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Homological Pisot Substitutions and Exact Regularity
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Pisot substitutions, exact regularity, and divisibility of coincidence rank by norms.
status_evidence.claim: Related conjecture (divisibility by a power of the norm) is studied; full conjecture not resolved.
